newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices rise despite improved supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices rise despite improved supply.

text.p: Sugar prices maintained their rise on Monday despite improved supplies, dealers said.
They said improved arrivals from local mills reduced the pressure on prices to some extent.
Demand from states adjoining India's western state of Maharashtra, of which Bombay is the capital, had pushed up prices sharply last week.
"Local supplies have improved with demand from other states coming down," said a dealer.

Ready sugar S-30 rose 15/25 rupees to 1,345/1,380 rupees per quintal and M-30 gained 10/20 rupees to 1,495/1,460 rupees per quintal. Mill delivery was up 5.0/15 rupees at 1,270/1,290 rupees per quintal.
Traders expect the market to remain firm because of growing demand for sugar by soft drink producers during the summer months of May and June.
